topic.name: EGFR
topic.short_description: Receptor tyrosine kinase - target for lung cancer therapy
topic.seo_title: EGFR Cancer Research - Latest Studies & Findings | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Learn about EGFR in cancer research. Explore targeted therapies, biomarkers, and diagnostic advances in lung cancer treatment and personalized oncology.
topic.seo_intro:
EGFR, or epidermal growth factor receptor, is a protein found on the surface of cells that plays a crucial role in cell growth and division. In cancer research, EGFR has emerged as one of the most important targets for developing precision therapies, particularly in lung cancer treatment. When cancer cells produce abnormal amounts of EGFR or develop mutations in the EGFR gene, these receptors can drive uncontrolled cell growth, making EGFR an ideal target for therapeutic intervention.

Over the past two decades, EGFR has revolutionized cancer care through the development of targeted therapies known as tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). These drugs are designed to specifically block EGFR signaling in cancer cells while minimizing damage to healthy tissue. For patients with EGFR-mutated lung cancers, these targeted therapies have significantly improved survival rates and quality of life compared to traditional chemotherapy. Beyond treatment, EGFR testing has become a critical diagnostic biomarker that helps oncologists identify which patients are most likely to benefit from specific targeted drugs, enabling truly personalized medicine approaches.

Current research continues to advance our understanding of EGFR biology, resistance mechanisms, and combination treatment strategies. This page features the latest peer-reviewed research on EGFR as a biomarker and diagnostic tool in cancer medicine, helping patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers stay informed about emerging discoveries and clinical applications.

articles.title: Review of Post-Study Clinical Endoscopy Reports in Follow Up to MAY2016-07-01 Weekly Erlotinib for Familial Adenomatous Polyposis
articles.hook: Weekly erlotinib delays polyp progression in familial adenomatous polyposis
articles.summary: Researchers reviewed endoscopy records to assess how quickly familial adenomatous polyposis progressed after patients stopped taking weekly erlotinib.

articles.title: A Phase 1/2, Open-label, Multicenter, First-in-Human Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Anti-tumor Activity of YH32364 in Patients With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors
articles.hook: YH32364 shows tolerability in EGFR-overexpressing advanced solid tumors
articles.summary: Researchers are testing YH32364, a new drug targeting EGFR-overexpressing advanced cancers in patients who failed prior treatment.

articles.title: A Phase Ib Dose Finding Study Assessing Safety and Activity of [177Lu]Lu-NeoB in Combination With Ribociclib and Fulvestrant in Participants With Estrogen Receptor Positive, Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-2 Negative and Gastrin Releasing Peptide Receptor Positive Advanced Breast Cancer Experiencing Early Relapse From (Neo)Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy or Who Have Progressed on Endocrine Therapy in Combination With a CDK4/6 Inhibitor for Advanced Disease
articles.hook: Lu-177-NeoB combined with ribociclib and fulvestrant targets hormone-receptor positive breast cancer
articles.summary: Researchers are testing a radioactive drug combined with two existing breast cancer medications to find the safe dose for hormone-receptor positive breast cancer.

articles.title: A Phase 3, Randomized Study of Amivantamab and Lazertinib Combination Therapy Versus Osimertinib Versus Lazertinib as First-Line Treatment in Patients With EGFR-Mutated Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.hook: Amivantamab and lazertinib combination outperforms osimertinib in EGFR-mutated lung cancer
articles.summary: Study tests whether combining amivantamab and lazertinib works better than standard osimertinib treatment for EGFR-mutated lung cancer.

articles.title: A Phase 2, Open-Label, Randomized Trial Evaluating the Impact of Enhanced Versus Standard Dermatologic Management on Selected Dermatologic Adverse Events Among Patients With Locally Advanced or Metastatic EGFR-Mutated NSCLC Treated First-Line With Amivantamab + Lazertinib
articles.hook: Enhanced dermatologic care reduces severe skin toxicity from amivantamab-lazertinib
articles.summary: Enhanced skin care management reduces severe skin side effects in lung cancer patients treated with amivantamab and lazertinib.

articles.title: A Phase 3, Randomized, Multi-center, Open-Label Study of DB-1303 Versus Investigator's Choice Chemotherapy in Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2)-Low, Hormone Receptor Positive (HR+) Metastatic Breast Cancer Patients Whose Disease Has Progressed on Endocrine Therapy (ET) (DYNASTY-Breast02)
articles.hook: DB-1303 outperforms chemotherapy in HER2-low breast cancer
articles.summary: DB-1303 is being tested against chemotherapy to treat hormone receptor positive, HER2-low metastatic breast cancer that has stopped responding to endocrine therapy.

articles.title: A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance.
articles.hook: KRAS-EGFR-STAT3 triple therapy eliminates pancreatic tumors and prevents drug resistance
articles.summary: Combining three targeted drugs—targeting KRAS, EGFR, and STAT3—completely shrinks pancreatic tumors and prevents treatment resistance.

articles.title: Rare EGFRm NSCLC: More First-Line Options Emerge.
articles.hook: Osimertinib-based combinations improve first-line outcomes in EGFRm NSCLC
articles.summary: Two new drug combinations show promise as first-line treatments for rare types of lung cancer with specific EGFR mutations.

articles.title: Elucidating the Mechanism of Oridonin in Treating Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
articles.hook: Oridonin blocks EGFR/PI3K/AKT pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma cells
articles.summary: Oridonin, a plant compound, fights liver cancer by blocking key proteins in the EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, stopping cell growth and triggering cell death.

articles.title: Who Truly Benefits from Anti-EGFR Rechallenge in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer? From Clinical Enrichment to ctDNA-Guided Molecular Hyperselection.

articles.summary: Anti-EGFR rechallenge benefits selected metastatic colorectal cancer patients with prior treatment response and absence of specific genetic mutations in blood tests.
